per_query.query: In hepatocellular carcinoma, what was found about macrophage migration inhibitory factor, and how did its knockdown affect tumor cell behavior and related protein expression?
per_query.reference: Macrophage migration inhibitory factor (MIF), a proinflammatory and immunoregulatory chemokine, plays important roles in cancer-related biological processes. In hepatocellular carcinoma tissues and cell lines, MIF and cyclin D1 expression levels were significantly upregulated compared with adjacent normal tissues or a normal liver cell line. In HCC specimens, MIF expression positively correlated with cyclin D1 expression, and both MIF and cyclin D1 expression positively correlated with tumor size. MIF knockdown inhibited the proliferation of PLC and HepG2 cells and promoted apoptosis, but small interfering RNA against MIF did not influence the cell cycle in these cells. In an in vivo xenograft model, MIF knockdown reduced the tumor growth rate. In MIF-knockdown cells, Bcl-2, p-caspase-3, BIM, and Bax were upregulated, while cyclin D1, p-Akt, and p-ERK were downregulated. These findings indicate that MIF siRNA reduces proliferation and increases apoptosis in HCC cells.

Human tumor necrosis factor (TNF)-alpha-induced protein 8-like 2 suppresses hepatocellular carcinoma metastasis through inhibiting Rac1 | Background Tumor invasion and metastasis are the major reasons for leading death of patients with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Therefore, to identify molecules that can suppress invasion and metastasis of tumor will provide novel targets for HCC therapies. Tumor necrosis factor (TNF)-alpha-induced protein 8-like 2, TIPE2, is a novel immune negative molecule and an inhibitor of the oncogenic Ras in mice but its function in human is unclear. Our previous research has shown that TIPE2 is downregulated in human primary HCC compared with the paired adjacent non-tumor tissues. Results In present study, we provide evidence that TIPE2 inhibits effectively human hepatocellular carcinoma metastasis. The forced expression of TIPE2 in HCC-derived cell lines markedly inhibits tumor cell growth, migration and invasion in vitro and suppresses growth and metastasis of HCC in vivo . Clinical information from a cohort of 112 patients reveals that loss or reduced expression of TIPE2 in primary HCC tissues is significantly associated with tumor metastasis. Mechanically, TIPE2 inhibits the migration and invasion through targeting Rac1 and then reduces F-actin polymerization and expression of matrix metallopeptidase 9 (MMP9) and urokinase plasminogen activator (uPA).

NASH and Hepatocellular Carcinoma: Immunology and Immunotherapy | Abstract The last 10 years have revolutionized our basic understanding of nonalcoholic fatty liver disease and consequent liver cancer. It has become clear that several innate and adaptive immune cells play an important role in initiating, maintaining, or exacerbating nonalcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH)—a disease that has been recently defined as autoaggressive. Despite improved disease management aimed at reducing the progression of fibrosis, NASH is set to become a leading cause for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Preliminary data from preclinical studies suggest that immunotherapy efficacy may be reduced in NASH-related HCC compared with viral HCC; however, conclusive evidence supporting clinical translation of these findings is lacking. Comprehensive clinical and immunologic phenotyping of mechanisms linking NASH progression with carcinogenesis and therapeutic resistance is key to prevent progression to cirrhosis, improve monitoring and stratification of NASH according to predicted cancer risk, and ultimately increase survival of patients with NASH-HCC. In this review, we summarize the state of the art in the field of NASH and NASH-HCC with focus on immunobiology. We discuss preclinical and clinical findings underpinning NASH as an immunologically distinct pro-tumorigenic disease entity, and explore areas of potential therapeutic vulnerabilities in NASH-associated HCC.

per_query.query: How are coronary artery calcifications associated with complications?
per_query.reference: Coronary artery calcification, visible on routine CT imaging, is independently associated with in-hospital complications and an adverse discharge condition in level-1 trauma patients. Left main coronary artery calcification was independently associated with the development of any complication (OR 3.9, 95% CI 1.7–8.9). An increasing number of calcified coronary arteries showed a trend toward an association with complications (p = 0.07) and was significantly associated with an adverse discharge condition (p = 0.02).

Median Injury Severity Score and Glasgow Coma Scale score were 9 and 15, respectively. Seventy-six patients suffered from at least one complication, mostly pneumonia ( n = 39, 9%) or delirium ( n = 19, 4%). Left main coronary artery calcification was independently associated with the development of any complication (OR 3.9, 95% CI 1.7–8.9). An increasing number of calcified coronary arteries showed a trend toward an association with complications ( p = 0.07) and was significantly associated with an adverse discharge condition ( p = 0.02). Pulmonary emphysema and aortic calcifications were not associated with complications. Conclusion Coronary artery calcification, visible on routine CT imaging, is independently associated with in-hospital complications and an adverse discharge condition in level-1 trauma patients. Coronary blood flow in heart failure: cause, consequence and bystander | Heart failure is a clinical syndrome where cardiac output is not sufficient to sustain adequate perfusion and normal bodily functions, initially during exercise and in more severe forms also at rest. The two most frequent forms are heart failure of ischemic origin and of non-ischemic origin. In heart failure of ischemic origin, reduced coronary blood flow is causal to cardiac contractile dysfunction, and this is true for stunned and hibernating myocardium, coronary microembolization, myocardial infarction and post-infarct remodeling, possibly also for the takotsubo syndrome. The most frequent form of non-ischemic heart failure is dilated cardiomyopathy, caused by genetic mutations, myocarditis, toxic agents or sustained tachyarrhythmias, where alterations in coronary blood flow result from and contribute to cardiac contractile dysfunction. Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy is caused by genetic mutations but can also result from increased pressure and volume overload (hypertension, valve disease). Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction is characterized by pronounced coronary microvascular dysfunction, the causal contribution of which is however not clear. The present review characterizes the alterations of coronary blood flow which are causes or consequences of heart failure in its different manifestations. per_query.final_answer: Across the supplied studies, coronary artery calcification is most consistently associated with worse clinical outcomes when it is measured directly on CT and used as a prognostic marker. In symptomatic patients referred for cardiac CT, absolute coronary artery calcium score had prognostic value for mortality, and higher calcification burden was linked to worse outcomes in that referred clinical setting [pmc_PMC9806039||ABSTRACT||000]. In another study, coronary artery calcification on routine CT was independently associated with in-hospital complications, with left main coronary artery calcification specifically linked to any complication and the number of calcified coronary arteries showing a trend toward complication risk and a significant association with adverse discharge condition [pmc_PMC10229702||ABSTRACT||001]. That study also found pulmonary emphysema and aortic calcifications were not associated with complications, suggesting the association was specific to coronary calcification rather than generalized calcific disease [pmc_PMC10229702||ABSTRACT||001]. A review also supports CAC as a predictor of future ASCVD risk independent of conventional risk factors, but emphasizes that no clinical trial has shown CAC screening improves clinical outcomes or healthcare costs, so its effect on complications is not proven in that sense [pmc_PMC5383538||ABSTRACT||000]. In severely calcified coronary lesions, calcification was associated with the need for orbital atherectomy and invasive imaging guidance, and plaque modification effects were common during the procedure [pmc_PMC10140256||ABSTRACT||000] [pmc_PMC10140256||ABSTRACT||001]. However, despite heavy calcification, that registry reported favorable short-term outcomes, with no primary safety events over 30 days, showing that severe calcification does not uniformly translate into immediate procedural complications [pmc_PMC10140256||ABSTRACT||001]. Overall, the evidence suggests coronary calcification is associated with higher risk of mortality, in-hospital complications, and more complex intervention, but the magnitude and type of risk vary by setting and measure of calcification [pmc_PMC9806039||ABSTRACT||000] [pmc_PMC10229702||ABSTRACT||001] [pmc_PMC10140256||ABSTRACT||001].

Case report Here, we report a novel case of a syndromic HNF1B -deficient paediatric patient that developed HCC with unique histopathological features characterised by neoplastic syncytial giant cells, which was observed only in one additional case of paediatric cholestatic liver disease of unknown origin. Conclusions Our case highlights the influence of HNF1B deficiency in liver disease progression and its putative association with a rare yet specific HCC histotype. We hypothesised that HCC could be secondary to the repressive effect of HNF1B variant on the HNF1A transcriptional activity.
